chunks: And 'Ammār al-Sābāṭī narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:
"When you stand for the obligatory salat (prayer), then recite the adhan and the iqamah, and separate between the adhan and the iqamah by sitting, or by speech, or by tasbih."
And he said: I asked him, "What is the minimum speech that suffices between the adhan and the iqamah?" He said: "Al-ḥamdu lillāh."

key_terms.أَقِمْ: pronounce the iqamah, the establishment of prayer
key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the adhan, the call announcing prayer
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the iqamah, the formula commencing prayer
key_terms.فَأَذِّنْ: give the adhan, the call to prayer
key_terms.يُجْزِي: is sufficient or fulfills the minimum requirement

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum that suffices between the adhan and iqamah in obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the etiquette of the adhan and iqamah before obligatory salat (prayer). It states that some separation should be made between them, even if minimal, and that the least sufficient phrase is saying "Al-ḥamdu lillāh."

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.877 - It is narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) by 'Ammar al-Sabati that He said: "When you stand for a mandatory prayer, give the adhan and the iqamah, and separate between the adhan and the iqamah with sitting, speaking, or tasbih (glorification of Allah (swt))."

He (Ammar) asked: "What is the minimum that suffices between the adhan and the iqamah in terms of speech?"
Imam (as) replied: "Saying 'Alhamdulillah' (All praise belongs to Allah (swt))."
